To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GABA transporters are localized within the astroglia and axons of GABAergic synapse in the mature cerebellar cortex and that GABA-uptaking system develops in parallel with synaptogenesis.

GABA-daicrine did not work during synapse formation, and that the onset of the GABA transporters expression was prior to synapse formation and that the GABA transport system was established when the synapses were sealed by the astrocyte process.

(1) the developmental expression of GAT- 1 and GAT 3 in the mouse cerebella was different from each other, and (2) the onset of GAT 1-expression was prior and the onset of GABT 3-expression was posterior to the synaptogenesis in the mouse cerebelum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the developmental changes in GAT-1 and 2 expression and their relationship to the development of the synaptic structure.
the developmental expression of GAT-2 in the cerebellar cortex and the formation of the GAT-2 system.
the development of GABAergic synapse in the mouse cerebelar cortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GABA-transporter system in the GABAergic synaptic transmission is formed during synaptogenesis in the mouse cerebelar cortex.
the GABA-transport system is formed during synaptogenesis in the GABAergic neurons and glia in the cerebellar cortex.
GABA-uptakes in the cerebellum are mediated by GAT-1 and 2 in the axon terminals and by GAT-3 in the glial cells, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABAergic synaptic transmission is initiated before the onset of GABA-uptakes in the GABAergic terminals and astrocytes.

GATs are localized within the GAT-3-positive astrocyte processes in the mature cerebellar cortex and that GAT-1 is localized within the axon terminals of the GABA neurons, which are presynaptic to GAT-3 positive astrocyte processes.
GABA-uptakes were not required for the GABAergic morphogenesis, but were necessary for the GABA-ergic synaptic functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both GATs start to localize within the synapses when they form.
the GABAergic system is formed in the cerebellar cortex by the expression of GAT-2 in GABAergic neurons and GAT-1 and 2 in astrocytes.
the GABA-transporter expression is developmentally regulated in the mouse cerebelar cortex.
